available_assertion.statement: For a number field F, a finite continuous discrete G_F-module M, and local subgroups L_v of H^1(F_v,M) equal to the unramified subgroup almost everywhere, the two dual Selmer groups are finite and |H^1_L(F,M)|/|H^1_Lperp(F,M^D)| = |H^0(F,M)|/|H^0(F,M^D)| times product_v |L_v|/|H^0(F_v,M)|.
available_assertion.objects: M^D=Hom_Z(M,mu_n) for nM=0, with contragredient Galois action; local annihilators use cup product and the local invariant map; all H^1 and H^0 in the displayed final formula are ordinary continuous Galois cohomology.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every number field F and every such finite continuous module and family of local conditions; all places occur in the product.
available_assertion.hypotheses: F is finite over Q; M has finite cardinality; local conditions are subgroups and are unramified except at finitely many places. The chosen finite exceptional set contains all archimedean places, all primes dividing |M|, and all ramification.
available_assertion.parameter_range: No condition that F be unramified at2; no odd-primary restriction. Includes modules of exponent2^j.
available_assertion.uniformity: An exact identity separately for each F,M,L; no uniform bound as these vary.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: At real places the intermediate Poitou–Tate sequence uses Tate H^0, but the final Euler-corrected formula uses ordinary H^0. At complex places H^1=0. Zero/full local subgroups have respectively full/zero H^1 annihilator.
available_assertion.constants: Every coefficient is explicit in the displayed cardinality identity; almost all product factors equal1.
available_assertion.normalization: The dual is the cyclotomic Tate dual, not the untwisted linear dual. For k-linear modules in characteristic2, the additive dual is identified with the k-linear dual twisted by1 using the nondegenerate finite-field trace.
available_assertion.limit_order: Choose the finite exceptional set for a fixed finite module and family of local conditions, apply the finite identity, then specialize. No passage to an infinite coefficient module is asserted.

connecting_derivation: Identify the finite Tate dual and the zero/full/unramified local conditions as in the nine comparisons. Apply published Theorem2.19 directly; no deduction of generality from the Q-only Theorem2.18 is needed. The theorem itself extends to arbitrary F.

comparisons.comparison: The theorem says number field; theta F is a totally real number field. Its ramification at2 is unrestricted.
All three theta modules are finite continuous additive G_F-modules; the theorem is not restricted to vector spaces or to exponent2.
Cyclotomic dual agrees with theta M^*(1); mu_(2^j) is retained for the constant cyclic module. In characteristic2 the mod2 cyclotomic action is trivial.
Zero at S, full at Q and unramified elsewhere satisfy the almost-everywhere condition. Local H^1 duality makes their annihilators full at S and zero at Q.
S includes every real place; ordinary H^0 remains in the final denominator. No vanishing of H^1(R,M) at2 is assumed.
The identity is a ratio of finite group orders. Taking log base |k| is allowed for the k-vector-space applications; no such linear-dimension replacement is made for Z/2^j.
For End_k(k^2), (X,Y) -> Tr_(k/F2)(tr(XY)) is nondegenerate and G_F-invariant. The presence of scalar trace-zero matrices in characteristic2 does not make this full-pairing degenerate.
This source input supplies the general finite identity, not theta cyclotomic disjointness, prime selection, tangent count, local module counts or class-field finiteness.
Published1995 Theorem2.19 p57 is inspected directly. The current author2007 Theorem2.19 p62 has the same needed statement. No equality of all2000/2007/1995bytes or1997reprint is asserted.
